column1: # Exact per-file ownership-diagnostic expectations for the direct-call carrier
# corpus. Columns: fixture, ObligationUnderReleased advisories, other blocking
# MIR findings, `hew check` exit code, runtime mode.
# Runtime modes and what each one proves:
#   check   the fixture is checked only (no `main` to execute, or a module root).
#   clean   the fixture is BUILT at -O2 and executed under the platform leak
#           oracle, and must report ZERO leaks.
#   leaks   the fixture is BUILT and executed the same way, and the oracle MUST
#           report a leak. These pin the demote-never-suppress rule: the leak is
#           real and the advisory is the only thing a user has. Silence the
#           advisory and the count column fails; close the leak and the oracle
#           fails at the lift event, at which point the row moves to `clean`.
#           A `leaks` row with zero advisories is refused structurally.
#   refuse  the fixture must produce a blocking MIR finding and a non-zero exit.
# Every executed fixture drives its shape at least 200,000 times. A per-call
# residue of one allocation is invisible at a single iteration, and refcounted
# shares of one string collapse into a single leak node — an executed fixture
# that calls its shape once can report zero leaks while leaking on every call.
# pO_alias.hew remains a counterexample: a `for` cursor over an owned-element
# `Vec` leaks two allocations per call, and its advisory is the only report of
# that. The validator must not fold its downstream binding into an ephemeral
# carrier that is absent from the balance model and thereby hide the leak.
